df['CustomerID'] = df['CustomerID'].astype(int)

# - InvoiceDate_x: string (keep as is, it is datetime string)

# The rest columns are integers, but some columns like InvoiceDate_y, InvoiceDate, Country_x, Country_y, UnitPrice_x, UnitPrice_y, Description_x, Description_y, Quantity_x, Quantity_y, StockCode_x, StockCode_y, InvoiceNo_x, InvoiceNo_y are currently numeric but may be float or object.

]

    # If column is not numeric, try to convert
    if not pd.api.types.is_integer_dtype(df[col]):
        df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)
    else:
        df[col] = df[col].astype(int)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = [
    'CustomerID', 'InvoiceDate_x', 'InvoiceNo_x', 'StockCode_x', 'Description_x', 'Quantity_x',

import pandas as pd

# Read source CSV with index_col=0 as per hint 21
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_14/training_0.csv", index_col=0)

# Perform self join on specified columns
joined = pd.merge(
    source0, source0,
    how='inner',
    left_on=["CustomerID", "InvoiceDate", "InvoiceNo", "StockCode"],
    right_on=["CustomerID", "InvoiceDate", "InvoiceNo", "StockCode"],
    suffixes=('_x', '_y')
)

# Group by the leftmost columns of the target schema that are string or integer and unique
group_cols = ["CustomerID", "InvoiceDate_x", "InvoiceNo_x", "StockCode_x"]

# Aggregation columns are all other columns except group by columns
agg_cols = [
    "Description_x", "Quantity_x", "InvoiceDate_y", "UnitPrice_x", "Country_x",
    "InvoiceNo_y", "StockCode_y", "Description_y", "Quantity_y", "InvoiceDate",
    "UnitPrice_y", "Country_y"
]

# Aggregate by sum for all aggregation columns
agg_dict = {col: 'sum' for col in agg_cols}

# Perform groupby and aggregation
result = joined.groupby(group_cols, dropna=False, as_index=False).agg(agg_dict)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = [
    'CustomerID', 'InvoiceDate_x', 'InvoiceNo_x', 'StockCode_x', 'Description_x', 'Quantity_x',
    'InvoiceDate_y', 'UnitPrice_x', 'Country_x', 'InvoiceNo_y', 'StockCode_y', 'Description_y',
    'Quantity_y', 'InvoiceDate', 'UnitPrice_y', 'Country_y'
]

result = result[target_columns]

# Write to target CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_14/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
